equity_bridge.item: Equity-method investment (minority stake retained from the 2022 industrial divestiture), carrying value
equity_bridge.note: Q2-2026 10-Q EquityMethodInvestments 1,792.2 at 2026-06-30; carried at book, not marked up. Its income is excluded from the operating flows.

equity_bridge.item: Less H1-FY2026 unlevered owner FCF already reflected in the June-26 net debt
equity_bridge.note: H1-26 OCF 1,061.6 - capex 25.3 - capitalised software 30.9 - SBC 108.2 = 897.2 levered owner FCF + after-tax H1 interest 210.7 x 0.78 = 164 -> ~1,060. Y1 projects full FY2026, so without this the first half is counted in both the flows and the net-debt reduction.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 7.4% vs revenue 3yr 13.7% (>30% divergence). Equity is distorted by the FY2022 Indicor/TransCore divestiture gain and by debt-funded M&A and 2026 buybacks; revenue CAGR is ~half acquired. Neither is an organic growth rate; organic runs ~5-6%.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2020-2025 on the continuing (post-industrial-divestiture) basis as restated in XBRL. EPS 3yr and owner-FCF 3yr are n/m: FY2022 EPS (42.92) carries the divestiture gain and FY2022 OCF (734.6) carries ~$1.4B of tax paid on that gain. Owner FCF = OCF - capex - capitalised software - SBC (no interest income stripped: Roper is net debt). Owner-FCF CAGR (10.5%) ~ reported FCF CAGR (10.4%): SBC has not been outgrowing cash flow. Historical growth is acquisition-funded (~$2-3.6B/yr of M&A FY2023-2025), which is why the forward path deducts that spend rather than extrapolating 10-14%.

scenario_narratives.base: Roper keeps doing what it says: ~6% organic growth in FY2026 (Application Software recurring revenue +7%, mid-90s gross retention) easing to 3% as the portfolio matures, margins edge up from 41.8% to 42.5% pre-SBC, and capital deployment returns from buybacks to M&A at ~15% of revenue a year at CentralReach-like ~7x revenue. Those deals are priced roughly at Roper's cost of capital, so they add revenue but little per-share value; the valuation is essentially the organic franchise plus near-neutral M&A, with the terminal value on organic economics only.
scenario_narratives.bull: The capital-allocation playbook keeps earning above its cost: organic growth holds at ~7% through Y5 on pricing, cross-sell (CBORD+Transact, Strata+Syntellis) and AI modules layered on embedded workflows, while the acquisition engine buys at ~6x revenue and lifts margins to 44%. Leverage is worked back down from ~3.5x by FCF. Terminal at 3.5% growth / 22x FCF reflects a durable vertical-software compounder.
scenario_narratives.bear: The two axes the bear case turns on both break: AI-native entrants and horizontal platforms erode pricing in some vertical niches and organic growth sinks to ~3%, with DAT and ConstructConnect adding cyclical drag; and serial-acquirer competition (Constellation, Thoma Bravo, Vista) pushes deal multiples to ~9x revenue so the same M&A spend buys far less growth, i.e. value-destructive. Margins slip to 40% as acquired businesses dilute and the debt-funded buyback leaves less flexibility. Terminal 2% growth at 15x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF of a serial acquirer in which acquisition growth is paid for: acquired revenue enters the growth path only with its purchase price deducted in the flows, and the terminal value capitalises organic economics only. SBC is fully expensed and the share count held flat; the equity-method stake is added at book and the H1-2026 cash already in the June balance sheet is removed from the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: M&A returns: the base assumes deals at ~7x revenue are roughly NPV-neutral; every 1x of multiple paid moves the value of the M&A layer materially
AI disruption of vertical-software pricing and retention (organic growth is the bulk of value)
Leverage ~3.4x net debt/EBITDA after debt-funded buybacks; refinancing at higher rates
Equity-method stake carried at book ($1.79B, ~$18/share) could be worth more or less on realisation

data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 882835): FY2023-FY2025 10-K and Q1/Q2-2026 10-Q -- revenue, operating income, D&A, SBC, OCF, capex (PaymentsToAcquireOtherProductiveAssets + PaymentsToDevelopSoftware), cash taxes paid, interest expense, debt, cash, equity-method investment, buybacks, cover-page share count; ROP_Metrics.csv for history
data_sources.qualitative: ROP_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): business model, FY2026 guidance (raised July 23 2026: adj DEPS $22.15-22.30, revenue growth >8%, organic ~6%), bull/bear points

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 98.90M basic on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-28) plus ~0.7M option/RSU treasury-method dilution (2.35M options outstanding at Dec-25, much of it near/out of the money at today's price; Q2-26 weighted diluted 100.6M is inflated by the in-quarter buyback timing). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. No non-SBC issuance modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back $166.3M (XBRL). Roper tags no net-share-settlement withholding line (awards are mostly options and RSAs settled gross); equity-award taxes treated as nil. H1-2026 SBC ran 2.57% of revenue, so the forward path starts at 2.5%, above the FY2025 2.1% anchor.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2025 OCF 2,540.3 less capex 47.4 (PaymentsToAcquireOtherProductiveAssets) less capitalised software 57.3 = 2,435.6. This is after ~$325M interest paid; the engine flows are unlevered and debt is deducted once via net_debt.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.95 -> cost of equity ~9.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (IG BBB+ notes) -> 3.8% after tax. Market weights ~77% equity ($36B) / 23% debt ($11B) -> ~7.8%; 8.0% used. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$59M/yr payments, $233.5M liability at Dec-25): lease cost sits inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route), per dcf-methods routing: Roper is an asset-light operating company (vertical-market software + technology-enabled products), not a holdco of minority stakes -- it consolidates 100%-owned businesses, so consolidated FCF is the owners' stream. First valuation of ROP (no MEMORY entry). SERIAL-ACQUIRER TREATMENT: acquisition-funded growth is NOT given away free. Revenue growth = organic (~6% FY26 guide, fading to 3%) + an explicit M&A layer, and the cash paid for that layer is deducted inside capex_pct (maintenance capex+capitalised software ~1.3-1.4% of revenue, plus acquisition spend of 5-15% of revenue in Y1-Y8 tapering to zero). Acquired revenue is priced at ~7x EV/sales in base (CentralReach/Procare/Syntellis-type multiples), 6x bull, ~9x bear; at the portfolio's ~32% owner-FCF margin that is a ~4.5% initial FCF yield growing with the acquired businesses -- i.e. close to NPV-neutral at an 8% WACC in base, value-creating in bull, value-destroying in bear. The M&A layer tapers to zero by Y9 so the terminal value capitalises an organic steady state (3% growth, maintenance capex only) rather than perpetuating either the M&A spend or the M&A growth. EBITDA margin is pre-SBC: FY2025 GAAP operating income 2,235.4 + D&A 898.2 + SBC 166.3 = 3,299.9 = 41.8% of revenue. D&A is ~91% acquired-intangible amortisation (858.4 of 898.2); the 22-23% cash tax rate is calibrated on EBIT after full D&A to reproduce FY2025 cash taxes (414.2 paid + ~68 interest shield = ~482 unlevered on 2,235 EBIT = 21.6%). BUYBACKS: Roper switched in H1-2026 from M&A to repurchases ($2,726.7M, 7.7M shares, debt-funded); value-neutral in this model at fair value, but it is why net debt rose to $10.95B and the count fell to 98.9M. TIMING: net debt is the 2026-06-30 balance, which already contains H1-2026 cash generation, while Y1 is full-year FY2026 flows; the H1 unlevered owner FCF is therefore removed in the equity bridge to avoid counting it twice. The Indicor-type equity-method stake (carrying value $1,792.2M at Jun-26, up from $963.6M after a $835M Q2 equity-method gain) is a non-operating asset added in the bridge; its income is not in the EBITDA used for the flows (operating income excludes equity-method income). Q2-2026 GAAP NI of $1,168.5M is dominated by that $835M equity-method gain and is not a run-rate.

bear.growth_rates_note: Organic slips to ~3.5-3.0 (AI-native competitors in vertical niches, DAT freight and ConstructConnect cyclicality), fading to 2.0; same M&A spend buys only ~1.7pp at ~9x EV/sales as Constellation/PE bid up targets.

base.growth_rates_note: Organic 6.0, 6.0, 5.75, 5.5, 5.25, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0 plus acquired contribution 2.5 (FY26 carry-over of CentralReach/Subsplash), then prior-year M&A spend / 7x EV-sales: 0.7, 2.1, 2.1, 2.1, 1.7, 1.3, 0.9, 0.4, 0. FY2026 total 8.5% matches 'north of 8%' guidance.
base.capex_pct_note: 1.4% maintenance capex + capitalised software, plus acquisition spend 5, 15, 15, 15, 12, 9, 6, 3, 0, 0 % of revenue (FY2023-25 actual M&A ran 33-51% of revenue; H1-26 only 0.7% as cash went to buybacks).

bull.growth_rates_note: Organic 6.5 -> 7.0 holding to Y5, fading to 3.5; acquired layer at 6x EV/sales (same spend, better prices / faster integration).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: net debt of ~$11B (~3.4x EBITDA) after debt-funded M&A AND a $2.7B debt-funded buyback, plus an unresolved AI-disruption question over vertical-software pricing. Base 50%: guidance was just raised and Q2 beat, so the organic franchise is tracking. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs two independent things -- sustained 7% organic and above-cost-of-capital M&A at lower multiples -- to go right together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
